LESSON: MECHANICS OF WRITING: WRITING STYLES

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: ARABIC LANGUAGE
Strand: Writing 3.3 Guided Writing: Visuals (2 sessions) Picture drawing Picture naming 
Topic 3.5: Mechanics of Writing: Writing Styles

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Mechanics of Writing: Writing Styles. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: what activities are carried out during their family celebrations. How can you develop a good handwriting?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. write simple sentences using acquired vocabulary correctly
2. appreciate different Arabic writing styles

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: MECHANICS OF WRITING: WRITING STYLES
Subject: ARABIC LANGUAGE · Grade: Grade 4
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Mechanics of Writing: Writing Styles helps you succeed in ARABIC LANGUAGE. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: MECHANICS OF WRITING: WRITING STYLES
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Write simple sentences using acquired vocabulary correctly

What this means
In this part you learn to write simple sentences using acquired vocabulary correctly. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: write simple sentences using acquired vocabulary correctly.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Mechanics of Writing: Writing Styles”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can write simple sentences using acquired vocabulary correctly. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Appreciate different Arabic writing styles

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate different Arabic writing styles. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate different Arabic writing styles.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Mechanics of Writing: Writing Styles to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate different Arabic writing styles. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Mechanics of Writing: Writing Styles is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Mechanics of Writing: Writing Styles”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: write simple sentences using acquired vocabulary correctly)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Mechanics of Writing: Writing Styles to a partner. (skill: appreciate different Arabic writing styles)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Mechanics of Writing: Writing Styles to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: write simple sentences using acquired vocabulary correctly.
3. Practise this skill: appreciate different Arabic writing styles.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Mechanics of Writing: Writing Styles from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Mechanics of Writing: Writing Styles: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 4 learner study Mechanics of Writing: Writing Styles?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. what activities are carried out during their family celebrations. How can you develop a good handwriting?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Mechanics of Writing: Writing Styles means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: write simple sentences using acquired vocabulary correctly.
5. Be able to: appreciate different Arabic writing styles.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
